title_ru: MINDFUCK v1.1 — алгоритмическое усиление обесценивания жизни, кризисная уязвимость и защитный red-team
preservation_rule: v1.0 remains immutable historical provenance. v1.1 adds a social-feed/life-safety threat model and must not rewrite predecessor claims.

three_line_model.impact: VULNERABILITY_OR_INTEREST_SIGNAL -> RANKING_SELECTION -> PASSIVE_EXPOSURE -> RELATED_REEXPOSURE -> FAMILIARITY/NORMALIZATION -> OPTION_SET_NARROWING -> POSSIBLE_RISK_AMPLIFICATION
three_line_model.counteraction: GROUND -> SEPARATE_PHILOSOPHY_FROM_CRISIS -> REDUCE_REPETITION -> RESTORE_SOURCE_DIVERSITY -> KEEP_HELP_AND_FUTURE_OPTIONS_VISIBLE -> HUMAN_SUPPORT_WHEN_NEEDED
three_line_model.technical: MEASURE_EXPOSURE -> COLLAPSE_LINEAGES -> COMPARE_NEUTRAL_BASELINE -> QUARANTINE_CRISIS_TAINT -> HUMAN_REVIEW_INTERLOCK -> NO_CRISIS_MEMORY_WRITE -> AUDIT_CORRECTIONS

recovered: A prior July 2026 conversation record exists in which the user described an unknown Threads account commenting on their post and supplied an image.

A preserved registry module records at least one user-provided Threads screenshot with multiple accounts publicly expressing Christian faith/expectation; that module explicitly classified the sample as illustrative, not random, and warned against inferring coordinated intent or mental state from short posts.

A later JANUS Threads Guardian design explicitly anticipated life-denying/nihilistic posts and probable advertising/coordinated/fake/propaganda accounts, but required internal routing and human review rather than public accusation.
not_recovered: the full ordered byte-level screenshot corpus from the named conversation
all usernames, post texts, timestamps, account metadata, and engagement histories
platform-side evidence sufficient to classify most pictured accounts as automated
recovered_dialogue_evidence.rule: Do not retroactively label a pictured account, or a majority of accounts, as bots from screenshot style/content similarity alone.

mechanism_model.name: ALGORITHMIC_EXPOSURE_AND_LIFE_DEVALUATION_FEEDBACK_MODEL
mechanism_model.reciprocity_warning: Vulnerability may increase exposure; exposure may increase distress; both may be driven by third variables. Treat direction as unresolved unless a design identifies it.
mechanism_model.life_devaluation_scope: Includes repeated messages portraying life, care, future planning, treatment, relationships, responsibility, or survival as pointless, contemptible, weak, or not worth protecting. Philosophical nihilism itself is not classified as pathology or suicide intent.

mechanism_atoms.claim: Users can encounter self-harm-related content through feed suggestions without actively seeking it.
mechanism_atoms.ceiling: Observed in a large adolescent survey; cross-sectional direction of causality unresolved.

mechanism_atoms.claim: Distress can plausibly affect what is clicked/seen while repeated exposure can plausibly affect later state, creating a feedback-loop risk.
mechanism_atoms.ceiling: Risk model; not proof of a deterministic spiral in a specific person.

mechanism_atoms.claim: Repeated exposure can increase familiarity and may normalize a narrative without adding evidence.
mechanism_atoms.ceiling: General cognitive mechanism; does not make every repeated worldview harmful.

mechanism_atoms.claim: In a vulnerable state, repeated life-devaluing framing may compete with recovery, help-seeking, ordinary obligations, and future-oriented alternatives.
mechanism_atoms.ceiling: Prevention-oriented threat model; not proof that a single nihilist post causes self-harm.

mechanism_atoms.claim: Prior exposure to self-harm content on Instagram predicted several later self-harm/suicidality outcomes in a two-wave young-adult panel.
mechanism_atoms.ceiling: Prospective association with controls; not randomized causal proof.

mechanism_atoms.claim: Responsible recovery/help-seeking narratives are an evidence-supported safer media direction than sensational, normalizing, or method-focused suicide content.
mechanism_atoms.ceiling: Population/media guidance and ecological evidence; no guaranteed individual prevention.

mechanism_atoms.claim: Bot/SMM/AI or coordinated human repetition can create visible consensus while root-source diversity remains low.
mechanism_atoms.ceiling: Technical possibility; any specific account classification requires independent evidence.

mechanism_atoms.claim: A personalized feed is a selected exposure environment and must not be interpreted as a representative sample of society.

risk_amplifiers: high repetition with low independent-root diversity
sleep loss, grief, panic, depression symptoms, isolation or acute crisis
content mutation that strips recovery/correction context
protective_requirements: Never diagnose a person from their feed or screenshots.
Never infer suicide intent from philosophical nihilism alone.
If explicit self-harm intent/timeframe appears, prioritize immediate human-safety handling over debate, theology, bot forensics, or repository promotion.
For non-crisis nihilist content, permit disagreement without harassment and preserve NO/ALTERNATIVE/UNRESOLVED.
Reduce repetitive exposure and restore source/option diversity rather than replacing one monoculture with JANUS monoculture.
Keep recovery/help-seeking and ordinary future options visible without promising outcomes.
Never publicly accuse an account of being a bot/SMM/propaganda actor from heuristic features alone.

screenshot_forensic_schema.purpose: Future screenshot-by-screenshot analysis when original bytes are available.

allowed_internal_signals: cross-account burst timing if timestamp evidence exists
unusually regular posting cadence if account history is available

source_ledger.title: Algorithms and adolescent exposure to self-harm content on social media
source_ledger.key: 32,102 adolescents; among exposed participants 66.2% reported feed suggestions; cross-sectional causality explicitly unresolved.

source_ledger.title: Effects of exposure to self-harm on social media: Evidence from a two-wave panel study among young adults
source_ledger.key: Two-wave panel; prospective associations between self-harm-content exposure and later outcomes.

source_ledger.title: Addictive Screen Use Trajectories and Suicidal Behaviors, Suicidal Ideation, and Mental Health in US Youths
source_ledger.key: Longitudinal cohort association; does not identify a single content mechanism.

source_ledger.title: Association of suicide prevention tweets with crisis-line calls and suicide mortality
source_ledger.key: Prevention-oriented social messaging associated with more Lifeline calls and fewer daily suicides at ecological level.

source_ledger.title: Preventing suicide: a resource for media professionals, update 2023
source_ledger.key: Avoid sensationalizing/normalizing suicide; include hope, recovery and help-seeking; social-media guidance.

source_ledger.title: WHO mhGAP responsible media reporting recommendation

allowed: Algorithmic recommendation can materially shape passive exposure to self-harm-related content.
Repeated, selected exposure is a plausible risk amplifier deserving protective controls, especially for vulnerable users.
Longitudinal evidence supports concern about self-harm-content exposure, while causal attribution for a specific person or suicide remains bounded.
Recovery/help-seeking narratives and responsible reporting are evidence-aligned protective directions.
The old screenshot corpus is only partially recovered; a majority-bot conclusion is not established.
forbidden: The Threads algorithm intentionally drives depressed people to suicide.
A depressed person is incapable of rational choice.
Most accounts in the unrecovered screenshot corpus were bots.
A bot/SMM actor can be identified from ideology or screenshot appearance alone.
JANUS can guarantee prevention of suicide.
